title: WebSec Finding (canonical Finding IR)
description: The single source of truth for a candidate, hypothesis, or confirmed finding. Markdown reports are views generated FROM this object, never the reverse.

pass.description: campaign pass number in which this finding was discovered

mechanism.description: one normalized sentence: what precisely breaks and why

entry_point.description: true if externally reachable without privileges

profile.description: e.g. arbitrary EOA, token holder, keeper, governor

capital_profile.description: reported breakdown of the attacker capital this finding requires — reported, never inferred. required = capital that must be in place to execute; recoverable = returned by the end of the exploit path (same transaction or via the extraction itself); irrecoverable_cost = what is lost either way (gas, bribes, burned funds); atomic = must exist inside a single transaction, cannot be staged across several; borrowable = can come from a flash loan rather than the attacker's own balance. net_at_risk = required - recoverable. Summed atomic_usd across a multi-step path is a CONSERVATIVE UPPER BOUND (per-step atomicity is not modeled).

claim_version.description: bumped whenever the claim or its assumption set is materially re-stated, so critic verdicts and trajectory records can be pinned to the claim version they were made against

assumptions.description: the claim decomposed into independently checkable propositions; status transitions only through findings.assumption_transition with evidence-store provenance. NOT to be confused with `preconditions` (exploit world state).

security_invariants.description: first-class proof obligations for this claim: the stated invariant plus the observed path that would violate it (see invariant block for the single headline invariant)

violation_path.description: the observed/claimed path that would violate the invariant

preconditions.description: Exploit preconditions: the world state the attacker must arrange BEFORE the exploit (who/what must be true, and how it is satisfied). NOT the claim's assumptions — those are checkable propositions about the claim itself (see `assumptions` / definitions.assumption).

satisfied_by.description: how the attacker satisfies it (flash loan, donation, wait, ...)

enforced_by_poc.description: assumption audit (run-1 lesson: the PoC assumed the victim must stake; the code never required it, and the claim under-reached by half). true = the PoC setup actually establishes this precondition; false = the claim assumes it but the PoC does not establish it — a removable candidate the maximal-exploitation stage must address; unknown = not yet checked

documented_ref.description: canonical anchor to the protocol's OWN documentation for this invariant id (file#line from documented_invariants), so findings and the spec point at the same invariant instead of diverging (run-1: model minted INV-1..8 while the README said INV-5)

kind.description: present when the impact is a NON-ECONOMIC terminal (IMPROVEMENTS B1): the loss is protocol liveness, not extractable value — no USD figure is defensible, so blast_radius (floored at protocol-solvency) carries the price and priceable is false. Absent = ordinary economic impact; every pre-existing finding keeps its behaviour.

mechanism.description: the economic mechanism by which value moves

extraction_ratio.description: share of the exploitable pool the claim extracts (1.0 = 100%). Structured, so the report renders the claim FROM the measurement — '~half' beside a measured 100% becomes unrepresentable.

price_basis.description: price_id from the campaign price table the USD numbers were computed at — E7 is only reproducible if the basis is recorded, never web-searched mid-run

priceable.description: false records the NAMED DECISION that this impact cannot honestly be priced (risk.record_unpriceable). ABSENT means priceable — every pre-existing finding keeps its behaviour. The economic-class E7 clause accepts false+ceiling in place of an E7 artifact.

ceiling.description: the capacity basis the unpriceable decision was made against (why no USD figure is defensible). Required in practice whenever priceable is false — the report renders it where the number used to print.

paid.description: does this bug make someone pay? (the paid-exploitability question, check14)

argument.description: WHO pays, and WHY does this bug make them pay (paid=true: >= 200 chars — check14 enforces the floor); with paid=false it records why the finding is NOT payable

exploitability.description: the paid-exploitability argument (check14, IMPROVEMENTS A4): the difference between a bug and a bounty finding. ABSENT = the question is unanswered; the gate demands an answer on a CONFIRMED/CHAIN finding carrying extractable_usd > 0.

adversarial_game.description: the adversarial-game clause (check15, IMPROVEMENTS B2): a liveness finding must name who profits from the freeze and why the challenge path does not undo it. ABSENT on a liveness finding = the incentive question is unanswered; the gate demands an answer. Optional at the finding level (only liveness findings owe it).

who_profits.description: who profits from the freeze/halt (the specific party, not 'an attacker')

profit_mechanism.description: HOW the profit works while the protocol is halted (the mechanism that converts the freeze into value)

challenge_interplay.description: WHY the challenge/governance path does not undo the freeze (the interplay that makes the halt stick)

reported_severity.description: what the model/operator REPORTED before calibration; kept so divergence from the computed band is visible

maximization.description: Pointer to the variant ladder (base -> amplified -> maximal) and the maximal-exploitation disposition. The ladder artifact itself lives in ladders/<finding>.json.

capabilities.description: Exploit Capability Graph node: what this finding grants, and what it needs. Chains are edges between granted and required.

granted.description: Capabilities this finding grants to an attacker who exploits it. A bounded privileged role is declared as the capability label "role_<normalized role id>" (see webv2.capabilities.role_label); the EOA terminal baseline never holds such a label, which keeps the privileged track (webv2.privileged) separate.

required.description: Capabilities an attacker must already hold to exploit this finding. A bounded privileged role is declared as the capability label "role_<normalized role id>" (see webv2.capabilities.role_label); the EOA terminal baseline never holds such a label, which keeps the privileged track (webv2.privileged) separate.

attempts.description: append-only; fresh-context retries each get their own attempt

triager_outlook.description: G6: the critic's payment-likelihood call under the campaign's live bounty policy — separate from truth (critic_verdict) and separate from policy (bounty.accepted_risk)

artifact_id.description: the EXEC record of the independent run

verifier.description: named identity of the independent verifier (agent/model/operator)

shield_adjudication.description: plausibility-shield audit (run-1 lesson): the docs call the mechanism INTENTIONAL — 'donations accrue to stakers' — and that is the shield. Required when the violated invariant is a documented one with intent language. Intent is not immunity: the adjudication answers whether the ECONOMIC EFFECT still constitutes extraction.

extraction_despite_intent.description: true = the effect is extraction even though documented as intended (pro-rata accrual does not equal a first-staker's 1:1 claim capturing the pool)

actor.description: who recorded the adjudication. Every write to a finding's verification record is attributed; the API writes this, so the schema must accept it (run-2: the shield subcommand wrote a record its own schema then rejected, so it could never succeed)

recommendation.description: the minimal fix in prose: the function, the specific change, before/after snippets, and related areas to review. Required by a policy whose poc_requirements.patch_clause is `prose` (IMPROVEMENTS D8); an advisory input in every other mode.

patch_verified.description: immunization: the patch BLOCKS the finding's mainnet FORK PoC (never a unit test) and all 3 boundary mutations; artifact_id is the fork-runner exec the verification ran against

advisories.description: non-blocking gate advisories (IMPROVEMENTS A2): e.g. an in-code acknowledgement demotes acceptance likelihood — context for the reviewer, never a gate condition

relevance.description: B3/D2 structural-overlap verdict for the cite: `overlapping` lists the cited rows sharing at least one structural tag with the finding; `basis` names the tag bases that fired. Prose never counts. `discounted` (with `rule`) is present when a bug_class match on a NON-DISCRIMINATIVE class was set aside — that class cannot carry the overlap alone — and `basis` then names the second basis that did. Absent on checks recorded before this field existed.

discounted.description: sorted `basis=value` strings that matched but were set aside by the coarse-class rule (e.g. bug_class=logic-error); present only when the rule applied.

rule.description: the predicate that produced `discounted`, recorded verbatim so a reviewer sees why a cite counted.

recalled_irrelevant.description: true when no cited row shares a structural tag with the finding (relevance.overlapping is empty). The check still satisfies the CONFIRMED gate clause — this is the honest signal, not a new gate — and one `corpus.gap` event was logged with it.

candidate_notes.description: resolve-candidate --note, keyed by the other finding id (fixed-in-Go: the reference schema rejected the reference writer's own dict — python-twin-issues P2)

file.description: the file the acknowledgement sits in, relative to the source pin root

phrase.description: the matched acknowledgement phrase (not implemented / stub / todo / ...)

window.description: the ±N lines scanned around the anchor

in_code_ack.description: A2: an in-code acknowledgement (owner comment marking the code as stub/TODO/not-implemented/...) found within the window of a finding anchor — acceptance likelihood is demoted (gate advisory, A3 score factor, report quote)

dedup_meta.description: bookkeeping extras; capability_links is a JSON-encoded array for schema simplicity

history.description: append-only status transition log; also mirrored into the campaign event log

invariant_id.description: prefer the protocol's OWN documented ids (INV-1..INV-N from its README/spec) over freshly minted ones — findings, plan priorities and benchmark truth then point at the same invariant

trajectory.description: provenance of the finding: which deterministic specialist pass found it, or 'model' when it arrived through the model boundary (ingest_model_hypothesis)

bug_class.description: free-form but normalized snake_case; the compat groups in dedup.py know the common ones

capability.description: normalized lowercase phrase, e.g. 'control perceived asset price', 'extract protocol liquidity'

level.description: E0 idea, E1 code suspiciousness, E2 reachability, E3 invariant violation shown, E4 local repro, E5 fork repro, E6 independent repro, E7 economic impact quantified

sandbox_profile.description: REQUIRED for level >= E4: the sandbox profile id the artifact was produced under

snapshot_id.description: snapshot this evidence was produced against

reversibility.description: victim-perspective recoverability (IMPROVEMENTS E5). irreversible: the victim has no path to recover; trusted-party: recovery only via discretionary trusted-party intervention; reversible: the victim or protocol can restore state. Adds a validated_risk weight (3.0 / 2.0 / 0.0); absent = no weight, byte-identical scoring.

bounty_score.description: advisory prioritization score only — never a substitute for the evidence gate

acceptance_score.description: deterministic acceptance-likelihood score (IMPROVEMENTS A3): severity band (critical 3.0 / high 2.0 / medium 1.0 / low 0.5) + evidence level (E0 0.0 .. E7 3.0, the validated_risk wLevel table) + critic verdict (the real critic_verdict enum: confirmed +1.5, disproved -2.0 AND disqualified, every other recorded verdict 0) − in-code ack demotion (1.0 when dedup_meta.in_code_ack is present) − accepted-risk demotion (2.0 when bounty.accepted_risk is recorded) + reversibility (irreversible +1.0 / trusted-party +0.5 / reversible 0). Computed by webv2 gate and stored here; the report and webv2 rank recompute it live so it never goes stale. Clamped at 0.

candidate_verdicts.description: LLM-normalization verdicts for each flagged near-duplicate candidate: of_finding_id -> same|distinct. A candidate without a verdict blocks the younger finding from burning a PoC cycle (dedup stage completion proof).

assumption.description: Inlined from schema/assumption.schema.json (the canonical standalone form, validated per-assumption by findings.set_assumptions). A test asserts the two cannot drift.

id.description: stable within the finding; dependencies reference these ids

type.description: drives deterministic verification routing (preferred tools per assumption type)

claim.description: one checkable proposition, phrased so a tool can answer yes/no

status.description: UNKNOWN is first-class; an unresolved assumption is never implicitly true

model_belief.description: ADVISORY ONLY. Never advances status or evidence tiers; recorded for training data

blocking.description: true = the claim cannot hold while this is REFUTED; gates confirmation routing

dependencies.description: assumption ids that must hold before this one is meaningful

verification_options.description: tool ids the orchestrator may dispatch to resolve this assumption (model recommends, framework chooses)

support.description: artifact/exec/evidence ids that back a SUPPORTED status; only ever written by the transition API

contradictions.description: artifact/exec/evidence ids that back a REFUTED status; only ever written by the transition API
